messages:
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for model-richgen-v2 on cluster:pool-phi (10 pods) — health-check window 30s, start 23:40:01 UTC

incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1 - elevated 5xx rate on /v1/inference for pool-phi canary (model-richgen-v2). auto-trigger threshold breached (5m). paging @jordan :pager:

jordan: ack — on it, pulling graphs now. any obvious error signatures?

maya: jumping in — cpu & mem look fine. LB shows a bunch of resets and http2 stream closes toward the canary pods. 5xx spikes ~12% at peak, sustained ~3m. logs show repeated: `backend error: connection reset by peer` and `pool exhausted` in runtime.

samir: linking runbook: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/canary-failures — likely connection-pool misconfig from latest config change. did the rollout include a conn limit bump?

jordan: yes, rollout included conn_pool_max=500 -> 1200 in runtime config for efficiency. maybe misbehaving w/ grpc mux.

maya: stack traces look like this:
```
2026-11-22T23:40:10Z runtime ERROR handleStream: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed
2026-11-22T23:40:11Z proxy WARN pool: no avail conns, queue len=78
2026-11-22T23:40:12Z runtime ERROR acceptConn: accept tcp: accept: connection reset by peer
```

jordan: ok, let's toggle the rollout kill-switch for the conn-pool flag first (less blast radius than full rollback). @deploy-bot can you flip `conn_pool_max` back to 500 for canary? command below.

samir: run `redwoodctl rollout update --target canary --set conn_pool_max=500 --reason "conn-reset spike"` — that should push the runtime flag without redeploy.

jordan: executing now:
```
$ redwoodctl rollout update --target canary --set conn_pool_max=500 --reason "conn-reset spike" --wait
Applying config to 10 canary pods... done.\n
```

deploy-bot: config change applied to canary pool-phi (10/10).

maya: metrics trending down to ~3% now after ~45s. latency normalizing but saw a small secondary blip.

carol: I'm seeing parity but still some 502s surfacing from edge for streaming sessions created during the spike window. recommend aborting the canary and rollback image to v1.13 to be safe.

jordan: agreed — kill-switch mitigated but not fully stable. initiating abort and rollback to v1.13.

jordan: rollback command (kubectl):
```
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/runtime runtime=ghcr.io/redwood/richgen:v1.13 --record
kubectl -n inference rollout status deployment/runtime --timeout=10m
```

ops-bot: canary abort initiated by jordan. traffic migration to baseline pool in progress.

deploy-bot: rollback completed, baseline image (v1.13) restored on pool-phi (10/10), healthchecks back to green.

maya: preliminary customer impact: ~7% of host API requests to /v1/inference received 5xx during the 4-minute window. No dedicated or private deployments affected. No data loss reported. We'll quantify exact Uptime SLA minutes and affected customers in postmortem.

jordan: good notes. I'm going to post an incident stub and timeline. handing off to @samir for postmortem and next steps (you’re on night shift). leave anything I missed in the incident doc. :thumbsup:

samir: taking it. I'll open incident doc + add timeline, graphs, and config diff. planning rollback root-cause triage tomorrow with runtime and infra. will add customer communication draft. acked.

carol: quick follow-up — capture pod-level tcp stats (conn resets) and gRPC client versions used by runtime; include in RCA.

jordan: noted. final status: canary aborted, rollback complete, customer impact contained, oncall handoff to samir. closing page.

incident-bot: Incident CLOSED by jordan at 23:41:32 UTC — severity lowered after rollback and traffic migration.
